question: Can Needle preserve binding CJEU holdings that alter or authoritatively constrain operative legal meaning without textual mutation?

cases.holding: Article 5(2) is invalid with effect from 21 December 2012.

functional_temporal_consequence.reason: Commission guidance states that from that date Article 5(1) applies without the Article 5(2) exception.

cases.holding: Consent for cookie storage/access is not validly constituted by a pre-checked checkbox that the user must deselect to refuse.
cases.temporal_guardrail: The judgment date is source/judgment time. This fixture does not invent 1 October 2019 as a new application start for the interpreted provisions.

change_atom_v0_3.reason: VERIFIED Change Atoms require one or more VERIFIED textual mutations; neither judgment textually mutates its target provision.

authoritative_finding_v0_1.reason: Authoritative Finding owns categorical determinations about concrete subjects/real-world conditions, not binding legal interpretation or invalidity of legal provisions.

temporal_v0_2.reason: Temporal can own the explicit Test-Achats derogation end boundary but does not own the judicial legal holding; Planet49 does not justify a new prospective temporal boundary.

source_observation.reason: Source observation can preserve judgment bytes/identity but not the binding legal proposition decided by the Court.

forbidden_inferences: The current consolidated text of Directive 2004/113 proves Article 5(2) remains legally available as a derogation.
The Test-Achats judgment is a textual mutation of Directive 2004/113.
LEGAL_FORCE must be used when a more precise functional DEROGATION end is evidenced.
Planet49 created Article 5(3) on 1 October 2019 or supplied a new application-start date.
A court's binding legal holding is a factual Authoritative Finding merely because it is an official determination.
Judgment publication time and the valid-time semantics of the interpreted rule may be collapsed.
